# US-03.2 — Keep the product working when BigQuery is unavailable

|                  |                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-03 Climate Telemetry & Ingestion](../epics/EPIC-03-climate-telemetry.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                             |
| **Estimate**     | 2                                                                              |
| **Status**       | Blocked                                                                        |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                |
| **Files**        | [backend/tools/climate_service.py](../../../backend/tools/climate_service.py)  |
| **Backlog ID**   | STORY-005 (EPIC-003)                                                           |
| **Requirements** | [FR-9](../../../agile/requirements.md); NFR-7, NFR-14                          |

## User story

**As an** operator,
**I want** analysis to continue with clearly labelled fallback telemetry when BigQuery is unavailable,
**so that** a cloud outage does not prevent heat assessment or masquerade as a real observation.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Cloud failures degrade gracefully**
Given missing credentials, quota exhaustion or a cloud network/query failure,
when telemetry is requested,
then it returns the documented reading shape with `source=fallback` instead of propagating the dependency failure.

**AC2 — Missing observations degrade gracefully**
Given an empty result or only missing-value rows,
when telemetry is requested,
then it returns labelled fallback data with maximum temperature between 35.0 and 41.0 Celsius and average temperature 5.0 to 7.0 Celsius lower.

**AC3 — Safe degradation diagnostic**
Given a dependency failure containing secret-like text or resource details,
when fallback is selected,
then a warning records degradation without credentials or a raw cloud error payload.

**AC4 — Programming defects remain visible**
Given an unexpected `TypeError` or `KeyError` from local reading handling,
when telemetry is requested,
then that defect is not concealed as a successful fallback observation.

## Tasks

- [x] Return a 38.5 Celsius maximum when the existing lookup fails or finds no rows
- [ ] Return the complete reading shape with explicit fallback provenance and an average
- [ ] Treat no valid rows, including filtered sentinels, as unavailable telemetry
- [ ] Catch specific cloud/authentication/query failures rather than every exception
- [ ] Replace printed raw exceptions with safe warning logging
- [ ] Add offline failure, empty-row, range and programming-error tests

## Current state

The skeleton's 38.5 Celsius fallback is within the required maximum range, but it is only a float. STORY-005 remains blocked on STORY-004.

| Defect                                                             | Impact                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No `source=fallback`, station/date metadata or average temperature | Consumers cannot label degraded telemetry or use the full FR-9 contract           |
| Blanket `except Exception`                                         | Local programming errors are hidden as apparently successful fallback readings    |
| `print` includes the raw exception                                 | Cloud error details may leak and logging cannot reliably identify degradation     |
| Sentinel rows are not excluded                                     | A missing reading can be returned as extreme heat rather than triggering fallback |

The epic's phrase "never raises" conflicts with its requirement that programming errors remain visible. Interpret it as no propagation of expected cloud/empty-data failures, consistent with the [GCP service instructions](../../instructions/gcp-services.instructions.md), not suppression of all bugs.

## Test cases

| Test                                                 | Asserts                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_cloud_failures_return_labelled_fallback`       | Credentials, quota and network/query errors produce the complete fallback shape        |
| `test_no_valid_rows_returns_plausible_fallback_pair` | Empty/sentinel-only results have a 35-41 Celsius maximum and 5-7 Celsius lower average |
| `test_fallback_warning_does_not_leak_cloud_payload`  | Captured warnings exclude secret-like content and raw errors                           |
| `test_programming_errors_are_not_hidden_by_fallback` | Local type/key defects still surface                                                   |

## Definition of done

All four cases pass without cloud credentials, fallback is visibly distinguishable from observation, expected dependency failures do not break analysis, and coverage meets the 70% floor. STORY-004 supplies the shared successful-reading shape; no second telemetry source is introduced.
